Container.Name: filearr
Container.Overview:
Unified media catalog and typo-tolerant search over mixed libraries (video, music, audiobooks, samples, images, 3D models, documents, spreadsheets). Scans filesystems directly; Postgres is the source of truth, Meilisearch a rebuildable search projection. Public REST API for search and metadata updates.
This ONE container runs both the web/API process and the background worker (scans, extraction, hashing, index sync, purge). That is what the 'all' in Post Arguments selects.
REQUIRES: the filearr-postgres and filearr-meilisearch containers (install first, or point the DSNs at servers you already run), and a network topology chosen up front.
NETWORKING — pick one before installing anything, because it decides what goes in the DSNs above. DEFAULT: every container on one user-defined Docker network named 'filearr' so they resolve each other by NAME; create it once in the Unraid terminal with docker network create filearr and leave the shipped DSN values alone. ALTERNATIVE: every container fully bridged (Network Type: Custom br0) with its own fixed LAN IP, and IPs in place of container names in Database URL, Procrastinate DSN and Meilisearch URL. Both are documented field by field, including the required DNS records and the br0 host-isolation gotcha: https://pwsh.github.io/filearr/deployment/unraid/#step-0-networking
First start bootstraps the database automatically (idempotent; waits for Postgres). Set FILEARR_AUTO_INIT_DB=false to manage migrations manually.
Full setup guide, including TLS and the distributed-agent fleet: https://pwsh.github.io/filearr/deployment/unraid/

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Web interface / API port

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: App data: thumbnails, caches, exports, uploaded agent releases

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Media library root (read-only; filearr never modifies files in v1). Library paths you create in the UI are IN-CONTAINER paths under this mapping, e.g. /data/media/movies.

Config.Name: Database URL
Config.Description: SQLAlchemy DSN (psycopg driver). Password must match filearr-postgres. Postgres 18 or newer is REQUIRED — filearr uses the native uuidv7() and refuses to start on an older server. Filearr assumes it owns the whole DATABASE (generic table names, the job queue shares the schema, and backups dump the database unfiltered), so give it a dedicated one.

Config.Name: Procrastinate DSN
Config.Description: Plain Postgres DSN for the job queue (same database, no driver prefix)

Config.Name: Meilisearch URL
Config.Description: Meilisearch endpoint. Tested against 1.53.x; 1.48.2 is the security floor, and older servers simply error on features filearr uses unconditionally (federated multi-search, _geo, /similar, embedders, searchCutoffMs).

Config.Name: Meilisearch Master Key
Config.Description: Must match filearr-meilisearch MEILI_MASTER_KEY. Filearr manages its own indexes and issues tenant tokens, so this key needs broad reach — sharing a Meilisearch with other apps is safe (filearr only touches indexes it owns) but the key is not narrowly scoped.

Config.Name: Auth Enabled
Config.Description: Login + API auth (default on; first visit shows the create-admin screen). Session cookies are Secure, so this needs HTTPS — set false only on a fully trusted LAN, or put the filearr-caddy container in front.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Envelope key encrypting alert-channel secrets (SMTP/webhook credentials). Optional until you use alerts (the API returns 503 without it). Generate: openssl rand -hex 32. Never rotate once set — and it is NOT inside a database dump, so record it separately or every stored channel secret becomes silently undecryptable after a restore.

Config.Name: Public Base URL
Config.Description: The URL clients actually reach this instance at, e.g. https://filearr.example.com. Optional — it is normally derived from the request and the proxy's X-Forwarded-* headers. Set it when that derivation is wrong: it is what agent install scripts, download links and report links are built from.

Config.Name: Recycle Retention Days
Config.Description: Days trashed items are kept before scheduled purge

Config.Name: Worker Concurrency
Config.Description: Parallel background jobs inside this container (extraction, hashing, thumbnails). Raise on a beefy box, lower if scans crowd out other Unraid work. Extract jobs run at negative priority so scan control always jumps the queue.

Config.Name: Worker Queues
Config.Description: Comma-separated queues this container's worker serves. EMPTY = all queues, which is what you want here — only set it (e.g. scan,index,maintenance) if you also run a second, extract-only container.

Config.Name: Stop Grace (seconds)
Config.Description: How long the container waits for the worker to finish in-flight jobs after SIGTERM before killing it. Must be ≤ the --stop-timeout in Extra Parameters, or Docker kills the container first and the grace never applies. 60 mirrors docker-compose.yml; the 10s default cut jobs off mid-transaction.

Config.Name: Postgres Data (disk monitor)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL read-only view of the filearr-postgres Data path, purely so the Jobs-page disk tile can watch the filesystem holding the database (and extraction can pause before filling it). Point at the SAME path as filearr-postgres's Data setting; remove this and the variable below to disable.

Config.Name: Postgres Disk Watch
Config.Description: In-container path of the Postgres data mount above (leave as /pgdata; clear to disable the database disk watch).

Config.Name: Semantic Search
Config.Description: Enables semantic/hybrid search; the worker downloads and loads a local ONNX embedding model and embeds items in the background. Safe default false (zero cost when off).

Config.Name: Hugging Face Token
Config.Description: OPTIONAL, only used with Semantic Search: a Hugging Face access token for the one-off embedding-model download (higher rate limit, no unauthenticated-request warning). Leave EMPTY (or type none) to download anonymously; a blank/placeholder value is never sent as a token. Never used for anything else.

Config.Name: Content Sniffing
Config.Description: Enables the on-demand maintenance action that reclassifies extensionless files by libmagic MIME sniffing (bounded prefix read per file). Safe default false.

Config.Name: Auto Update Check
Config.Description: Lets the Jobs-page Updates card refresh its stale GitHub release cache automatically; this is the only automatic outbound call the product makes. Safe default false (manual check still available).

Config.Name: Thumbnail Budget (GiB)
Config.Description: Advisory size budget for the thumbnail cache in GiB; over it you get a log reminder and an amber note on the Jobs thumbs card — nothing is deleted. 0 disables the advisory. Safe default 5.

Config.Name: Log Recorder
Config.Description: Records the application log stream into the database so the console Logs panel has content. Safe default true; set false to keep logs in the container output only.

Config.Name: Distributed Agents
Config.Description: Master switch for the distributed agent fleet surface (remote scan agents, enrollment, agent API). The agent API 404s and the Agents page is hidden until this is true. Safe default false.

Config.Name: Agent Auth Mode
Config.Description: How enrolled agents authenticate: fingerprint (agent presents its certificate fingerprint over any transport — no proxy needed), mtls-header (only a verified client certificate terminated by the filearr-caddy container is accepted), or both (migration window; flip to mtls-header once every agent shows the mTLS badge). mtls-header and both FAIL CLOSED without Proxy Shared Secret below.

Config.Name: Proxy Shared Secret
Config.Description: SECRET. The value filearr-caddy stamps on X-Filearr-Proxy-Auth / X-Filearr-Proxy-Trust, proving a request really transited the proxy rather than being forged against port 8484. Lets filearr trust the proxy's X-Forwarded-For (real client IPs in the security audit, sessions and login rate limit) and is required for Agent Auth Mode mtls-header/both. Must be byte-identical here and on the filearr-caddy container. Generate: openssl rand -hex 32.

Config.Name: Agent Plane URL
Config.Description: Where enrolled agents talk to central: the filearr-caddy mTLS agent site, https://agents.<domain>. Handed to each agent at enrolment (agents bootstrap via the console URL because the mTLS site demands a certificate they do not have yet), so an mtls-header deployment needs no per-agent repoint. Leave empty on fingerprint-only deployments.

Config.Name: CA URL
Config.Description: step-ca bootstrap URL handed to registering agents, e.g. https://ca.example.com. Must be reachable BY THE AGENTS (the raw layer-4 passthrough on filearr-caddy), not just from this container.

Config.Name: CA Root Fingerprint
Config.Description: step-ca root certificate fingerprint, pinned into the registration response so an agent can bootstrap trust without a pre-shared root file. Read it from the filearr-stepca container log on first boot, or: docker exec filearr-stepca step certificate fingerprint /home/step/certs/root_ca.crt

Config.Name: CA Provisioner
Config.Description: Name of the step-ca JWK provisioner filearr mints one-time tokens against. Must match DOCKER_STEPCA_INIT_PROVISIONER_NAME on the filearr-stepca container.

Config.Name: CA Provisioner JWK
Config.Description: SECRET, on a par with Secret Key. The provisioner's DECRYPTED private JWK (a JSON object) — it is what lets filearr mint the short-lived ca_ott an agent uses to get its own certificate from step-ca. Without it registration still succeeds but ca_ott is null and enrollment cannot complete. Extraction procedure: see the Unraid deployment guide.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID (Unraid default: 99/nobody)

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID (Unraid default: 100/users)

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone (affects scan schedules)
